body_md:
Canadian police drama Saint-Pierre has emerged as a major domestic television success. According to Numeris audience data cited in a November 2026 report, the series was CBC's most watched drama of the 2025–26 television season and ranked among Canada's most popular shows. Its performance illustrates how a crime story rooted in a distinctive local community can develop appeal beyond its original market.

Allan Hawco plays Donny Fitz Fitzpatrick, a Royal Newfoundland Constabulary inspector whose investigation brings him too close to a corrupt politician. Reassigned to the French islands of Saint Pierre and Miquelon near Newfoundland, he finds himself working alongside Deputy Chief Geneviève Arch Archambault, played by Joséphine Jobert. Their contrasting investigative styles provide a central source of dramatic tension.

Fitz relies heavily on instinct and practical experience, while Arch is more analytical, guarded and sarcastic. The series uses a mystery-of-the-week structure but combines its approachable procedural format with darker themes and more complicated human relationships. Viewers familiar with Death in Paradise or Shetland may recognize elements of both traditions without finding an identical formula.

Hawco conceived the project while scouting locations for another production. He subsequently developed the series with Robina Lord-Stafford, sharing showrunning responsibilities while also acting, writing and producing. For Hawco, the island setting is not simply an attractive backdrop. Its geography and community helped inspire the concept and remain fundamental to the show's identity.

Production is divided between St. John's and Saint-Pierre, creating logistical challenges alongside the usual difficulties of financing Canadian television. Hawco has highlighted the importance of international partnerships and regional tax incentives, including support available in Newfoundland and Labrador. He credits the wider creative and production team with helping the series achieve its ambitions within a comparatively modest budget.

International distributor Fifth Season has secured agreements across several territories, including the United Kingdom, France, Australia and New Zealand. Despite that progress, a United States distribution deal had not been announced at the time of the report. Hawco remains optimistic that the series will eventually find an appropriate American home.

Meanwhile, production on the third season is already well underway. New cast members Assaad Bouab and Caroline Dhavernas are expected to introduce fresh dynamics to the established ensemble. An exact premiere date was not provided. The continuing production and international sales suggest that the small island at the heart of Saint-Pierre still has plenty of stories to offer audiences.
